test_title: SSC Selection Post 2025 (Matriculation Level) Official Paper (Held On: 01 Aug, 2025 Shift 1)
subject: general
question: Which author won the Booker Prize for the novel "The God of Small Things"?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Arundhati Roy**__.

**__Key Points__**
__

• **Arundhati Roy** (born **November 24, 1961**) is a world-renowned Indian author who won the prestigious **Booker Prize** for Fiction in **1997** for her debut novel, **'The God of Small Things'**. She was the first **resident Indian citizen** to receive this honor. ***Hence, the correct answer is Arundhati Roy.***

• **Ruskin Bond** (born **May 19, 1934**) is an iconic Indian author of British descent, famous for his children's literature and stories set in the **Himalayas**. Although he won the **Sahitya Akademi Award** in **1992** for **'Our Trees Still Grow in Dehra'** and the **Padma Bhushan** in **2014**, he has never won the **Booker Prize**. ***Hence, this option is incorrect.***

• **R.K. Narayan** (**1906–2001**) was one of the most celebrated Indian novelists writing in English, best known for creating the fictional South Indian town of **Malgudi**. While he received the **Sahitya Akademi Award** in **1958** for his novel **'The Guide'**, he did not win the **Booker Prize**. ***Hence, this option is incorrect.***

• **Anita Desai** (born **June 24, 1937**) is a distinguished novelist who has been **shortlisted** for the **Booker Prize** three times for her works **'Clear Light of Day'** (**1980**), **'In Custody'** (**1984**), and **'Fasting, Feasting'** (**1999**). Despite these nominations, she has not won the award, though her daughter, **Kiran Desai**, won it in **2006**. ***Hence, this option is incorrect.***

**Additional Information__**
__

• **'The God of Small Things'**: The novel is set in **Aymanam**, **Kottayam** district, **Kerala**, **India**. It tells the story of fraternal twins **Rahel** and **Estha** and explores how childhood experiences shape their adult lives. The book is noted for its exploration of the **caste system**, **communism**, and the **'Love Laws'** that dictate who should be loved and how.

• **The Booker Prize**: Established in **1969**, it is a literary prize awarded annually for the best original novel written in the **English language** and published in the **United Kingdom** or **Ireland**. It is considered one of the most influential literary awards globally.

• **Arundhati Roy's Activism**: Following her literary success, **Arundhati Roy** became a prominent **political activist**. She has written extensively on **human rights**, **environmental issues**, and **globalization**. She was notably involved in the **Narmada Bachao Andolan** alongside **Medha Patkar**.

• **Literary Achievement**: **'The God of Small Things'** was an immediate commercial and critical success, reaching the top of the **New York Times Bestseller** list. It has been translated into over **40 languages** worldwide.

**Important Points__**

• **Other Indian Booker Winners**: Apart from Roy, other authors of Indian origin who have won the **Booker Prize** include **V.S. Naipaul** (**1971** for **'In a Free State'**), **Salman Rushdie** (**1981** for **'Midnight's Children'**), **Kiran Desai** (**2006** for **'The Inheritance of Loss'**), and **Aravind Adiga** (**2008** for **'The White Tiger'**).

• **Salman Rushdie's Special Honor**: His novel **'Midnight's Children'** was uniquely honored with the **'Booker of Bookers'** in **1993** and the **'Best of the Booker'** in **2008** to mark the prize's **25th** and **40th** anniversaries, respectively.

• **International Booker Prize**: It is important to distinguish the **Booker Prize** from the **International Booker Prize**. In **2022**, **Geetanjali Shree** became the first Indian author to win the **International Booker Prize** for her novel **'Tomb of Sand'** (originally **'Ret Samadhi'**), which was translated from **Hindi**.

• **Roy's Second Novel**: After a gap of **20 years**, **Arundhati Roy** published her second novel, **'The Ministry of Utmost Happiness'**, in **2017**. It was also longlisted for the **Booker Prize** that year.
